resources.barrier_detail: No barrier. einfo.fcgi?db=gds returned HTTP 200 (dbbuild Build260930-1932.1, 9,085,330 records). All 59 esearch.fcgi and all esummary.fcgi/acc.cgi calls returned HTTP 200. No CAPTCHA, no rate-limit 429, no login wall.
resources.notes: CORE NEGATIVE FINDING, stated plainly: GEO contains NO dataset in which human platelets, platelet-rich plasma, washed platelets, or human megakaryocytes/megakaryocytic progenitors are exposed to an oligonucleotide. 'phosphorothioate AND platelet' = 0 records. 'TLR9 AND CpG oligonucleotide AND platelet' = 0. 'platelet AND antisense oligonucleotide' = 2 records, both false positives (GSE286091 is mouse atherosclerosis with an apoB ASO where 'platelet' is phenotype not assay substrate; the other hit is platform GPL1261). 'megakaryocyte AND antisense oligonucleotide' = 1 record, which is platform GPL1261 only. I inspected titles for all 52 hits of 'platelet AND oligonucleotide', all 39 of 'megakaryocyte AND oligonucleotide' and all 31 of 'thrombocytopenia AND oligonucleotide': every one is a false positive driven by (a) the word 'oligonucleotide' in 'oligonucleotide array'/'oligo-dT'/'oligonucleotide-labeled cells (CITE-seq/HTO)', (b) 'oligodendrocyte' stem-matching, or (c) MeSH explosion of 'platelet' to Blood Platelets in studies with no oligo exposure. Human thrombocytopenia datasets exist (GSE273786 and GSE290319 CYCS variant, GSE206089 ETV6-related, GSE574/GDS390 ITP) but none involve oligonucleotide exposure, so they do not serve this endpoint. I verified querytranslation for every broad hit to make sure counts were not MeSH artefacts: 'gapmer'=1481, 'phosphorothioate'=304, "2'-O-methoxyethyl"=57 all translate to [All Fields] literally, and manual inspection shows these are overwhelmingly cell-line or rodent tissue studies, not blood. Priority-drug searches: drisapersen, PRO051, aprinocarsen, ISIS 3521, ISIS 5132, alicaforsen, ISIS 2302, donidalorsen, olezarsen, mipomersen, fomivirsen, golodirsen, viltolarsen, casimersen ALL return count=0 - these drugs have no GEO footprint at all. oblimersen/G3139/Genasense return 6 records which are all false positives (DLBCL methylation GSE23501/GSE23967 and radiation biodosimetry GSE58613; the term matches author/methods text, not an oblimersen exposure arm). pelacarsen returns 1 record (GSE249911) which is Lp(a) lipidomics in monocytes with no pelacarsen exposure arm. volanesorsen returns 1 mouse apoC-III record (GSE131284). eteplirsen's single hit (GSE130182) is a myotonic-dystrophy myoblast AON study that merely cites eteplirsen in its summary. The three genuinely useful records are human in vitro ASO-exposure transcriptomics in NON-platelet cells and are reported as candidates. Negative finding on two named priority papers: Sewing 2017 (PLOS ONE pone.0187574) and Slingsby 2022 (PMID 33567808) have NO GEO accession - 'Slingsby AND platelet' = 0, and the 'Sewing' query instead surfaced a different Roche paper (GSE83392, Moisan 2017 OMTN, S. Sewing co-author). So the per-donor raw data for those two papers must be sought in their journal supplements, not here.

resources.resource: NCBI SRA (Sequence Read Archive, E-utilities db=sra)
resources.barrier_detail: No barrier. All 39 esearch.fcgi?db=sra and esummary.fcgi?db=sra calls returned HTTP 200. No CAPTCHA, no 429, no login wall. SRA run-level fastq/BAM download was NOT attempted (prefetch/fasterq-dump not run); only the Entrez metadata layer was queried.
resources.notes: SRA contributed NO independent discovery for this endpoint; its only value was resolving raw-read project accessions for studies already found in GEO. Honest query-by-query account: 'platelet AND antisense oligonucleotide' = 0, 'platelet AND phosphorothioate' = 0, 'megakaryocyte AND antisense oligonucleotide' = 0, 'megakaryocyte AND oligonucleotide' = 0, 'antisense oligonucleotide AND thrombocytopenia' = 0, 'thrombocytopenia AND oligonucleotide' = 0, 'platelet factor 4 AND antisense' = 0, 'steric blocking antisense oligonucleotide' = 0, "2'-MOE" = 0 (SRA free text does not index the prime/hyphen form). Every named priority drug returns 0 except nusinersen (110 runs, all neural/fibroblast models) and G3139 (6 runs). I checked all 6 G3139 runs by esummary and every one is a false positive: a 16S metagenomic sample literally named 'G3139', a WGS isolate 'CRBC_G3139', a Sesamum indicum accession 'G3139-1', a conifer capture library, and an NIDDK T2D WGS library - the string is a specimen label, not oblimersen. The large counts are likewise unusable as-is: 'platelet AND oligonucleotide' = 586 runs, and the three I spot-checked by esummary were a mouse pMCAO brain scRNA-seq, a 10x run whose methods text says 'oligonucleotide labeled cells', and a plasma miRNA-seq run - i.e. the term matches library-prep chemistry, not drug exposure. 'platelets AND human[ORGN] AND RNA-Seq[Strategy]' = 7310 and 'megakaryocyte AND human[ORGN] AND RNA-Seq[Strategy]' = 786 are untargeted platelet/MK transcriptomics with no oligonucleotide arm; I did not enumerate these because SRA free text cannot express 'exposed to an oligonucleotide' and the GEO side already establishes that no such human platelet study is deposited. Useful resolutions: PRJNA1519705 = 84 SRA runs backing GSE345276 (cASO control-ASO panel); PRJNA1321660 = 20 SRA runs backing GSE307431 (2'-OMe/PS vs 2'-MOE/PS vs PMO triad). Note the asymmetry I observed and am recording rather than smoothing over: searching db=sra for the literal string 'GSE307431' returns count=0 while its BioProject PRJNA1321660 returns 20 - GEO series IDs are not reliably indexed in SRA free text, so BioProject must be used as the join key. PRJNA325783/SRP076607 for GSE83392 was read from the GEO Series_relation field, not from an SRA query.

candidates.full_title: To scramble or not: steric blocking 2'-MOE/PS control antisense oligonucleotides across cellular models
candidates.authors_year: Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids, 2026 (vol 37, art. 103051); GEO submission 2026
candidates.discovered_via: NCBI E-utilities esearch db=gds, query "oligonucleotide toxicity" and "2'-MOE antisense"; identity confirmed by esummary db=pubmed on PMID 42733805 returning DOI 10.1016/j.omtn.2026.103051
candidates.publisher_or_repo: NCBI GEO / NCBI SRA (public, no embargo; GEO data are free to redistribute)
candidates.required_file: Per-sample sample-characteristics table from acc.cgi?acc=GSE345276&targ=gsm&form=text (gives the cASO arm label for every replicate) plus GSE345276_RAW.tar (17,305,600 bytes, HTTP 200 at https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE345nnn/GSE345276/suppl/GSE345276_RAW.tar) or the 84 SRA runs under PRJNA1519705
candidates.endpoint_gap_it_closes: This is the GEO/SRA deposit of the exact paper named in the priority list as the source of the cASO7/cASO9/cASO11 sequences (doi:10.1016/j.omtn.2026.103051). I VERIFIED by enumerating all GSM titles that the series carries discrete cASO1, cASO2, cASO3, cASO4, cASO5, cASO7, cASO8, cASO9, cASO10, cASO11, cASO12, cASO13, cASO14, cASO15, cASO17, cASO18, cASO19 arms at 4 replicates each, plus 8 TransIT-X2 vehicle controls and an untreated arm (84 samples total). It therefore gives an independent, machine-readable confirmation that cASO7/9/11 are real distinct 2'-MOE/PS steric-blocking control entities and supplies per-replicate transcriptome-wide off-target burden for each of them - the quantitative counterpart to the Table S2 sequence list. Dose and duration are fixed and explicit in the record: 100 nM, TransIT-X2 at 3:1 reagent:ASO, 48 h incubation.
candidates.expected_usable_observations: 84 per-replicate human transcriptome samples = 17 cASO arms x 4 replicates + 8 vehicle + untreated, all HEK293T. NOTE the limitation I checked rather than assumed: although the series summary claims seven cellular models (HEK293T, HeLa, NIH/3T3, SH-SY5Y), every one of the 84 GSM titles in this accession reads 'HEK293T cells', so the HeLa/SH-SY5Y/NIH-3T3 arms are NOT in this accession and must be sought in the paper or a sibling deposit.

candidates.full_title: A therapeutic antisense oligonucleotide encompassing 2'-O-methoxyethyl modification triggers unique perturbation of the transcriptome
candidates.discovered_via: NCBI E-utilities esearch db=gds, queries "phosphorothioate", "nusinersen", "phosphorodiamidate morpholino" and "2'-O-methyl phosphorothioate AND Homo sapiens[ORGN]" (all four converge on this accession); PMID resolved to DOI via esummary db=pubmed
candidates.required_file: GSE307431_Counts.csv.gz - DOWNLOADED to staging (see notes for filename/bytes/sha256). Raw reads: 20 SRA runs under PRJNA1321660.
candidates.endpoint_gap_it_closes: Closes the backbone/2'-chemistry comparator gap directly, and does it in a matched-sequence design that is rare: the SAME ISS-N1 target sequence delivered as F18OMe (2'-O-methyl, phosphorothioate), F18MOE (2'-O-methoxyethyl, phosphorothioate) and F20PMO (phosphorodiamidate morpholino, NEUTRAL backbone), each with its own scrambled control (ScrOMe, ScrMOE, ScrPMO) and an untreated arm. The priority list asks for 'PMO class as the neutral-backbone comparator'; this is a human-cell dataset in which PS and non-PS backbones are isolated as the only variable, so any PS-backbone-specific transcriptional signature (the mechanism most often invoked for PS-oligo platelet effects) can be separated from sequence effects. It also anchors the 2'-OMe/PS chemistry class of drisapersen, for which no GEO record of the drug itself exists.
candidates.expected_usable_observations: 20 per-replicate human transcriptomes. I confirmed the exact arm structure from the downloaded counts header: Untreated, ScrOMe, F18OMe, ScrMOE, F18MOE, ScrPMO, F20PMO across replicates 1-3 (replicate 2 lacks an Untreated column), 7 arms x 3 replicates minus 1. Cells are GM03813 SMA patient skin fibroblasts, 6 uM ASO by Lonza 4D nucleofection (primary cell P2 kit, EN-150), harvested 24 h post-nucleofection. Gene-level counts are Ensembl-ID keyed with chr/start/end/strand/length annotation, 43,266,261 bytes uncompressed.

candidates.full_title: Molecular phenotyping of antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) in immortalized proximal tubule epithelial cells (PTEC-TERT1) [GEO series for: Inhibition of EGF Uptake by Nephrotoxic Antisense Drugs In Vitro and Implications for Preclinical Safety Profiling]
candidates.authors_year: Moisan A, Gubler M, Zhang JD, Tessier Y, Dumong Erichsen K, Sewing S, Gerard R, Avignon B, Huber S, Benmansour F, Chen X, Villasenor R, et al., 2017
candidates.discovered_via: NCBI E-utilities esearch db=gds, query "Sewing AND antisense oligonucleotide" (run specifically to hunt for a GEO deposit behind Sewing 2017 PLOS ONE pone.0187574); PMID resolved to DOI and author list via esummary db=pubmed
candidates.publisher_or_repo: NCBI GEO / NCBI SRA (public); study is Roche, same group as the named Sewing 2017 PLOS ONE paper (S. Sewing is a co-author here)
candidates.required_file: GSE83392_ASO-MolecularPhenotyping.gct.gz - DOWNLOADED to staging (see notes). Raw reads under SRP076607 / PRJNA325783.
candidates.endpoint_gap_it_closes: Partial, indirect: supplies a human in vitro, per-replicate, DOSE-RESOLVED ASO toxicity transcriptomics matrix with per-ASO identity (5 named ASOs: PCSK9-B, PCSK9-C, PCSK9-D, Myd88-E, Scramble-A) at 10/30/100 uM against vehicle, 3 biological replicates, +/- exogenous EGF. Its value to a thrombocytopenia dataset is as a sequence-dependent-versus-chemistry-dependent human toxicity reference and as a dose-response shape for individual ASOs - the challenge's 'extrapolate between in vitro human systems' criterion. BE CLEAR ABOUT WHAT IT IS NOT: the cells are kidney proximal tubule epithelium, there is no platelet or megakaryocyte readout, and no platelet count. It is a supporting comparator, not thrombocytopenia evidence.
candidates.expected_usable_observations: 107 samples (confirmed from the .gct header line '1035 107'), 1035 pathway-reporter genes quantified by targeted amplicon NGS, condition labels embedded per column in the form NNN_<ASO>_<conc>_<EGF status>. Design per GEO: 5 ASOs x 3 concentrations x +/- EGF x 3 biological replicates plus vehicle controls, 6 h exposure.

notes:
Resource family: ncbi_omics. Search date recorded: 2026-10-02 (sweep executed 2026-10-03 UTC; the challenge-specified search date is used in the search_date fields as instructed). Two resource rows, one for GEO and one for SRA, not merged. 98 distinct Entrez queries were actually executed (59 against db=gds, 39 against db=sra) plus esummary and GEO acc.cgi metadata retrievals. BARRIERS: none. Every HTTP request in this sweep returned 200. There was no CAPTCHA, no human-verification page, no rate limiting, no login wall and no paywall anywhere in GEO, SRA, Entrez E-utilities or the NCBI FTP-over-HTTPS supplementary endpoints. No API key was used and none was required at the request rates used (0.4-0.5 s spacing). I am recording zero barriers because zero occurred, not because I did not look.

HEADLINE HONEST ASSESSMENT, so no reader over-reads this file: GEO and SRA contain NO human platelet and NO human megakaryocyte dataset under oligonucleotide exposure. Not one. This is the single most important output of this sweep and it is a negative. 'phosphorothioate AND platelet' returns 0 records in GEO and 0 in SRA. The resource family is therefore close to NOT_APPLICABLE for the primary endpoint (oligonucleotide-induced thrombocytopenia with a platelet readout), and I considered marking it so; I marked both rows 'results' instead only because three genuine human in vitro ASO-exposure transcriptomics datasets were found that serve the chemistry-characterisation half of the task. I did not pad the result list with the thousands of untargeted platelet-transcriptome runs that SRA will return, because none of them has an oligonucleotide arm and counting them would misrepresent the search.

WHY THE BIG COUNTS ARE NOT RESULTS, verified not assumed: I checked querytranslation on every broad query to rule out MeSH-explosion artefacts, and I inspected record titles or esummary payloads for the hits that mattered. 'platelet AND oligonucleotide' (GEO 52, SRA 586) and 'megakaryocyte AND oligonucleotide' (GEO 39) are false positives generated by library-prep language ('oligonucleotide array', 'oligo-dT', 'oligonucleotide-labeled cells' in CITE-seq/HTO protocols), by 'oligodendrocyte' stem-matching, and by MeSH expansion of 'platelet' to Blood Platelets in studies with no oligo exposure. All 6 SRA hits for 'G3139' are specimen labels (a 16S metagenome named G3139, a bacterial isolate CRBC_G3139, a Sesamum indicum accession G3139-1, a conifer capture library, an NIDDK T2D WGS library), not oblimersen. The 6 GEO hits for oblimersen/G3139/Genasense are DLBCL methylation and radiation-biodosimetry series with no oblimersen arm.

PRIORITY DRUGS WITH ZERO OMICS FOOTPRINT (count=0 in both db=gds and db=sra, worth knowing so no one searches here again): drisapersen/PRO051, aprinocarsen/ISIS 3521, ISIS 5132, alicaforsen/ISIS 2302, donidalorsen, olezarsen, mipomersen, fomivirsen, golodirsen, viltolarsen, casimersen. pelacarsen, volanesorsen, inotersen and eteplirsen each return 1-13 records, all of which I checked and none of which contains an exposure arm for that drug. Nusinersen returns 110 GEO and 110 SRA records, all neural or fibroblast models with no haematological readout.

NAMED PAPERS CONFIRMED ABSENT FROM THESE REPOSITORIES: Sewing 2017 (PLOS ONE pone.0187574) and Slingsby 2022 (PMID 33567808) have no GEO or SRA accession - 'Slingsby AND platelet' returns 0 in GEO. Their raw/per-donor data must be pursued through the journal supplements, which is outside this resource family. The 'Sewing' query did surface a different and useful Roche paper, GSE83392 (Moisan 2017, PMID 28325303, S. Sewing co-author), reported as candidate 3; I am flagging explicitly that this is NOT the Sewing 2017 PLOS ONE paper, to prevent a mis-crosswalk downstream.

BEST FINDING: GSE345276 / PRJNA1519705 is the GEO+SRA deposit of doi:10.1016/j.omtn.2026.103051, the very paper the priority list names as the source of the cASO7/cASO9/cASO11 control sequences. By enumerating all 84 GSM titles I confirmed discrete cASO1-5, cASO7-15, cASO17-19 arms at 4 replicates each (cASO6 and cASO16 absent), so cASO7, cASO9 and cASO11 are independently corroborated as distinct entities with per-replicate transcriptome data at a stated 100 nM / 48 h exposure. Caveat I verified rather than glossed: the series summary advertises seven cellular models but all 84 samples in this accession are HEK293T, so the HeLa, SH-SY5Y and NIH/3T3 arms are not here.

JOIN-KEY GOTCHA for whoever reuses this: GEO series accessions are not reliably indexed in SRA free text. esearch db=sra for 'GSE307431' returns count=0 while its BioProject PRJNA1321660 returns 20 runs. Always join GEO to SRA via the BioProject/SRP in the GEO !Series_relation field.
